resolution_contract.canonical_profile_id: Use the exact public catalog identity. Normalize semantic-type, capability, and historical fixture aliases before rendering.
resolution_contract.default: After semantic routing, select the one canonical or anchor profile whose canonical_parent equals the routed type unless the user explicitly selects a compatible capability or presentation profile.
resolution_contract.ambiguity: If two compatible profiles remain materially distinct after applying the trusted request, ask the user; do not choose by styling preference.
resolution_contract.unsupported: Fail closed. Never substitute a generic layout or a different profile silently.
resolution_contract.custom_structure: Only an explicit safe user request may set structural_override to custom-structure; disclose that the output is outside the 45-profile contract.
resolution_contract.fallback: Always declare fallback. Use null when none occurred; otherwise name the requested and delivered profile and explain the reason.

allowed_without_structural_override: element or series count within the profile semantic boundary
renderer_may_reflow: expand repeated rows, columns, ranks, lanes, layers, or series
split presentation while preserving declared continuity
must_preserve: connector endpoints, ports, direction, route family, continuity, arrowheads, crossings, junctions, guards, returns, and clearance

ledger_contract.claim_boundary: A valid binding proves identity and provenance only. Structural conformance still requires checks against the actual arrangement, marks, ports, routes, arrows, crossings, junctions, overlap, and clipping.

engine_grammars.axis: dependency flow across ordered trust or responsibility zones
engine_grammars.placement: nodes stay inside their owning zone and align by dependency rank; branches form subordinate ranks rather than a free card grid
engine_grammars.ports: boundary-facing side ports; distribute multiple edges along the side
engine_grammars.routes: continuous orthogonal routes with rounded corners unless the selected profile says otherwise
engine_grammars.crossings_junctions: avoid crossings; declare shared trunks or junctions and never imply connection by accidental contact
engine_grammars.reflow: add rank space or widen zones while preserving zone order and dependency direction

engine_grammars.axis: source to transform/platform to consumer or sink
engine_grammars.placement: stages form ordered columns; platform or transform boundaries enclose owned services
engine_grammars.ports: east-west transfer ports with boundary crossings attached to the owning stage
engine_grammars.routes: continuous directed transfer routes, orthogonal when lanes or boundaries require them
engine_grammars.crossings_junctions: fan-in and fan-out use explicit distributed ports or declared junctions
engine_grammars.reflow: expand stage columns, stack peers within a stage, and preserve lineage order

engine_grammars.axis: runtime communication across nested zone, host, and artifact containment
engine_grammars.placement: artifacts remain inside hosts and hosts inside zones; peer zones keep a stable reading order
engine_grammars.ports: connect exact artifact or host boundaries, never a nearby decorative container
engine_grammars.routes: directed runtime routes outside labels and container titles
engine_grammars.crossings_junctions: route around containment and declare any shared endpoint
engine_grammars.reflow: grow containers from child bounds and preserve placement hierarchy

engine_grammars.axis: acyclic rank progression with explicit separated cycle back-edges when present
engine_grammars.placement: nodes occupy dependency ranks; fan-in and fan-out remain visually legible
engine_grammars.routes: forward edges follow rank direction; cycle edges use a distinct outer return corridor
engine_grammars.crossings_junctions: minimize crossings and never merge independent edges without a declared junction
engine_grammars.reflow: add ranks or increase rank gaps without changing dependency order

engine_grammars.axis: ordered directed flow with semantic branch and return structure
engine_grammars.placement: start or initial state precedes activities or states; terminals close each reachable branch
engine_grammars.ports: role-aware ports on process, decision, state, and terminal marks
engine_grammars.routes: directed orthogonal branches; guards stay on their edge; return routes use a separated corridor
engine_grammars.crossings_junctions: branch and merge points are explicit; crossings never imply merge
engine_grammars.reflow: add ranks and branch space while preserving guards, reachability, and direction

engine_grammars.axis: ownership or participant order on one axis and chronology or handoff progression on the other
engine_grammars.placement: each activity stays in its lane or each message stays between its participant lifelines
engine_grammars.ports: lane-boundary or lifeline endpoints with exact sender and receiver roles
engine_grammars.routes: handoffs use continuous orthogonal routes; messages use straight horizontal routes; self-calls use a rounded return
engine_grammars.crossings_junctions: preserve chronological order and keep unrelated messages visually separate
engine_grammars.reflow: expand lanes or chronology depth without changing ownership, participant order, or message order

engine_grammars.axis: one disclosed chronological or calendar scale
engine_grammars.placement: events, tasks, and milestones align to their actual position or interval
engine_grammars.ports: leaders attach event marks to labels; dependencies attach task boundaries
engine_grammars.routes: time rail is not a semantic connector; dependencies route outside task bars
engine_grammars.crossings_junctions: offset labels and dependency corridors instead of crossing data marks
engine_grammars.reflow: extend the time domain or row count without distorting duration or chronology

engine_grammars.axis: ordered work or journey stages across columns with aligned semantic rows
engine_grammars.placement: items stay in their status, journey stage, backbone activity, or release slice
engine_grammars.ports: connect only when the profile declares progression or handoff semantics
engine_grammars.routes: default is position-carried meaning; optional progression rails do not connect unrelated cards
engine_grammars.crossings_junctions: avoid connector crossings by using aligned rows and columns
engine_grammars.reflow: add columns, rows, or cards while preserving WIP, stage order, and release cuts

engine_grammars.placement: each child sits below its parent span; sibling order is stable
engine_grammars.ports: parent distribution bus to child top ports, or direct centered parent-child ports
engine_grammars.routes: tree routes are continuous and directionally consistent
engine_grammars.crossings_junctions: shared distribution buses are explicit; unrelated branches do not touch
engine_grammars.reflow: widen sibling spans and add ranks while preserving parentage

engine_grammars.axis: ordered containment depth, layer order, or tier progression
engine_grammars.placement: children remain within parents; layers or tiers keep their declared order
engine_grammars.ports: cross-layer routes attach the exact layer or item boundary
engine_grammars.routes: no connector when enclosure or shared boundary carries the meaning; otherwise use directed cross-layer routes
engine_grammars.crossings_junctions: keep routes outside labels and declare shared transitions
engine_grammars.reflow: grow enclosing bounds or repeat layers and tiers without changing order or containment

engine_grammars.axis: entity, table, or class peers arranged for relationship legibility
engine_grammars.placement: headers and member rows remain inside one compartment; related peers align where practical
engine_grammars.ports: relationships bind exact compartments or member rows with independent endpoint labels
engine_grammars.routes: typed relationship or foreign-key routes preserve multiplicity and endpoint semantics
engine_grammars.crossings_junctions: avoid shared ambiguous trunks; crossings do not imply relationship
engine_grammars.reflow: grow compartments from member count and add rows or columns without detaching endpoints

engine_grammars.axis: two disclosed dimensions, set regions, or row-column position
engine_grammars.placement: marks remain at their semantic coordinate, cell, or membership region
engine_grammars.ports: only relationship-bearing profiles use exact node ports
engine_grammars.routes: axes and region boundaries are not connectors; leaders are non-semantic unless declared
engine_grammars.crossings_junctions: dependency crossings remain separate; overlap is meaningful only for set profiles
engine_grammars.reflow: expand scale, grid, or region labels without changing coordinates, cells, or membership

engine_grammars.axis: one or more disclosed quantitative scales with data-faithful mark placement
engine_grammars.placement: marks derive from values, ranks, domains, or distributions rather than decorative spacing
engine_grammars.ports: only profile-declared comparison segments or trend paths connect marks
engine_grammars.routes: axes and gridlines are not arrows; data paths preserve series continuity and missing-value semantics
engine_grammars.crossings_junctions: series crossings do not imply junction; direct labels identify series and endpoints
engine_grammars.reflow: extend domains, categories, series, or rows while preserving scale and value encoding

engine_grammars.axis: profile-specific conserved flow, cause spine, or closed cycle geometry
engine_grammars.placement: marks occupy the profile's declared interfaces, spine branches, or ring stations
engine_grammars.ports: attach exact ribbon interfaces, cause branch endpoints, or cycle station ports
engine_grammars.routes: preserve ribbon continuity and width, angled cause convergence, or one-direction closed-cycle flow
engine_grammars.crossings_junctions: conservation interfaces and shared spines are explicit; unrelated paths never merge silently
engine_grammars.reflow: grow interfaces, branch spacing, or ring radius while preserving the special geometry

profiles.arrangement: Parallel vertical trust-zone columns ordered from external edge through application to content or data; dependency ranks progress left to right and fan-out targets stack within their owning zone.
profiles.containment: Every component is fully contained by exactly its owning trust zone; zone labels and boundaries remain visually distinct from component cards.
profiles.rank_order: External entry rank, application service ranks, then content or data rank; siblings sharing a predecessor stay aligned as a branch.
profiles.marks: Rounded component card with compact role badge, primary label, and optional secondary line; focal origin may be emphasized without changing shape.
profiles.connectors: Directed east-to-west-boundary dependency routes using distributed side ports, continuous rounded orthogonal paths, target arrowheads, explicit branch separation, and no label or boundary collision.
profiles.reading_order: Zone order first, then dependency rank, then top-to-bottom siblings.
profiles.reflow: Widen zones or add aligned sibling rows; never replace the zone topology with a generic card matrix.
profiles.forbidden: Uncontained nodes, diagonal spaghetti, hard-corner branch drift, center-to-center edges, silent zone reorder, or free-floating legend marks.

profiles.arrangement: Sources occupy the left stage, transformations or platform services the middle stage, and consumers or sinks the right stage; peers stack within their stage.
profiles.containment: Platform-owned services may share a bounded middle container; sources and consumers stay outside it unless semantically owned.
profiles.rank_order: Lineage rank is source then transform/platform then sink; fan-in and fan-out preserve exact source-target relations.
profiles.marks: Source, transform, service, and sink cards retain distinct role badges or shapes.
profiles.connectors: Directed transfer routes attach east-west ports, cross boundaries explicitly, and keep one continuous source-to-target path per relation.
profiles.reading_order: Left-to-right lineage, then top-to-bottom peers within a stage.
profiles.reflow: Add stage width or peer rows while keeping the three-stage pipeline and lineage.
profiles.forbidden: Generic equal cards without role, backward silent flow, detached boundary crossings, or merged unrelated transfers.

profiles.arrangement: Peer runtime zones form ordered regions; hosts sit inside zones and deployed artifacts sit inside hosts.
profiles.containment: Zone to host to artifact nesting is mandatory and replicas remain visibly associated with their placement.
profiles.rank_order: Placement hierarchy precedes communication order; peer zones follow the request's environment or trust order.
profiles.marks: Zone boundary, host container, deployed artifact card, and replica or runtime badge are distinct marks.
profiles.connectors: Runtime communication connects exact artifact or host ports, crosses container boundaries cleanly, and uses directional arrowheads when the relation is directed.
profiles.reading_order: Outer zones, hosts within each zone, artifacts within each host, then communications.
profiles.reflow: Grow parents from child bounds and add hosts or replicas without flattening containment.
profiles.forbidden: Artifacts outside hosts, hostless replicas, edge attachment to decorative zone centers, or topology replaced by a flat network.

profiles.arrangement: Dependencies advance through discrete ranks; fan-in and fan-out remain visible, while any true cycle uses an outer separated return corridor.
profiles.containment: Optional groups enclose complete dependency subgraphs without hiding rank order.
profiles.rank_order: Topological rank determines primary placement; stable sibling order avoids unnecessary crossings.
profiles.marks: Dependency nodes use one consistent bounded node vocabulary with optional role or state badge.
profiles.connectors: Forward directed edges use rank-facing ports; cycle back-edges are visibly distinct, continuous, arrowed, and routed outside forward ranks.
profiles.reading_order: Rank progression, top-to-bottom siblings, then declared back-edges.
profiles.reflow: Add ranks or widen fan-out spans; never pull a successor into an earlier rank for compactness.
profiles.forbidden: Undeclared cycles, ambiguous merged edges, arrowless directed dependencies, or free-force placement.

profiles.arrangement: A clear primary flow advances through ordered ranks; decision branches separate and each reachable branch ends or rejoins explicitly.
profiles.containment: Optional subprocess or phase boundaries enclose complete steps and do not cut through connectors.
profiles.rank_order: Start precedes activities and decisions; branch outcomes retain a consistent yes/no or guard order; terminals close the flow.
profiles.marks: Terminator, activity rectangle, decision diamond, document or artifact, and terminal marks are role-specific.
profiles.connectors: Directed orthogonal paths use role-aware ports, arrowheads, guard labels on their own edge, and explicit merge or return corridors.
profiles.reading_order: Primary flow first, branch order second, returns last.
profiles.reflow: Increase branch and rank spacing or change overall orientation only when all role and guard semantics remain intact.
profiles.forbidden: All-card vocabulary, unlabeled decisions, disconnected terminals, edge-label ambiguity, or crossings that imply merge.

profiles.arrangement: Parallel ownership lanes contain their activities; process progression crosses lanes only at actual handoffs.
profiles.containment: Each activity is fully inside one lane and lane labels remain separate from activity content.
profiles.rank_order: Activity order follows the process axis; lane order follows named owners, not visual convenience.
profiles.marks: Lane bands, activity cards, event or decision marks, and handoff labels are distinct.
profiles.connectors: Within-lane flow and cross-lane handoffs use continuous rounded orthogonal paths, exact boundary ports, target arrows, and declared guards.
profiles.reading_order: Process progression first, then lane ownership at each rank.
profiles.reflow: Grow lane height or process width and wrap within a lane without moving work to another owner.
profiles.forbidden: Floating activities, diagonal lane hops, erased connector segments, implicit handoffs, or lane reorder.

profiles.arrangement: One chronological rail carries proportionally placed event markers; labels alternate or stack off the rail to preserve legibility.
profiles.containment: Optional phases occupy non-overlapping spans behind or beside the rail without changing event dates.
profiles.rank_order: Strict chronological order with simultaneous events aligned to the same time position.
profiles.marks: Time rail, event or milestone marker, leader, date label, and event text block.
profiles.connectors: The rail expresses time rather than causality; leaders are non-arrowed and causal dependencies, if present, are separately styled and declared.
profiles.reading_order: Earliest to latest, with same-time events in stable request order.
profiles.reflow: Extend the domain or alternate label rows; never equal-space non-equal dates when a proportional scale is claimed.
profiles.forbidden: Decorative equal spacing under a numeric time claim, arrowed leaders, or event reorder.

profiles.arrangement: Journey stages form ordered columns while actions, touchpoints, thoughts, pain points, and sentiment align in semantic rows.
profiles.containment: Every observation belongs to one stage and one row; stage headers span their full column.
profiles.rank_order: Stage chronology left to right; row order follows the journey vocabulary; sentiment uses the same stage alignment.
profiles.marks: Stage header, moment card, touchpoint badge, note, and sentiment point or curve.
profiles.connectors: A progression rail may link stage headers; sentiment is a continuous series, not a process connector.
profiles.reading_order: Stage by stage, then aligned rows within each stage.
profiles.reflow: Add stages or row depth while preserving column alignment and the sentiment scale.
profiles.forbidden: Unaligned cards, sentiment used as decoration, shuffled stage order, or a generic kanban board.

profiles.arrangement: The primary leader or role occupies the top rank and reports fan out into centered subordinate spans below.
profiles.containment: Optional department groups enclose complete subordinate branches without obscuring reporting lines.
profiles.rank_order: Management depth determines rank; sibling order is stable and secondary relations do not displace the primary tree.
profiles.marks: Role cards with title and optional person or unit metadata.
profiles.connectors: Primary reporting uses centered parent-to-distribution-bus-to-child routes or direct centered routes; secondary relations are distinct and declared.
profiles.reading_order: Top leader, then each rank left to right.
profiles.reflow: Widen sibling spans and add ranks while retaining centered parentage.
profiles.forbidden: Force graph layout, crossed primary reporting lines, multiple undeclared parents, or hierarchy inferred by card position alone.

profiles.arrangement: A single continuous tapered silhouette is divided into ordered tiers whose width or area communicates progression or magnitude.
profiles.containment: Tier labels and values stay within their tier; shared tier boundaries carry order.
profiles.rank_order: Broad-to-narrow or narrow-to-broad order follows the declared funnel or pyramid semantics.
profiles.marks: Continuous outer silhouette, internal tier boundaries, tier labels, and values.
profiles.connectors: No node-to-node arrows by default; tier adjacency and shared boundaries express progression.
profiles.reading_order: Declared entry tier through terminal tier.
profiles.reflow: Add or resize tiers proportionally while preserving one continuous silhouette and tier order.
profiles.forbidden: Disconnected stacked cards, decorative arrows between tiers, reversed order, or widths unrelated to a claimed quantitative value.

profiles.arrangement: Database tables are peer compartments arranged to expose foreign-key relations with minimal crossings.
profiles.containment: Table header, columns, keys, and indexes remain inside one table compartment; member rows retain their order.
profiles.rank_order: Referenced or parent tables precede dependent tables when possible; member order follows the source schema.
profiles.marks: Table compartment with header and typed rows; PK, FK, nullability, and index badges are distinct.
profiles.connectors: Foreign-key routes bind exact source and target column rows, carry endpoint roles or multiplicity, and avoid ambiguous shared trunks.
profiles.reading_order: Table dependency order, then top-to-bottom rows inside each table.
profiles.reflow: Grow table height and column gaps from row count; never detach a foreign key from its row.
profiles.forbidden: Generic entity cards without columns, center-to-center FK lines, lost key roles, or relationship crossings treated as junctions.

profiles.arrangement: Two perpendicular disclosed axes create four named regions; observations occupy positions derived from their two values.
profiles.containment: Region labels stay in their quadrant and do not cover observations.
profiles.rank_order: Position follows x and y values; label priority determines annotation order, not point position.
profiles.marks: Axis, grid or midpoint divider, positioned point, direct label, and optional region wash.
profiles.connectors: Axes are non-semantic and leaders are non-arrowed; observations are not connected unless the source declares a relation.
profiles.reading_order: Axis labels and scale, quadrant names, then observations in stable order.
profiles.reflow: Expand domains and move labels while preserving each observation's relative coordinate.
profiles.forbidden: Equal card grid, arrowed axes presented as causal flow, arbitrary point placement, or quadrant reorder.

profiles.arrangement: A rectangular x-y plotting field places independent observations at their exact two-dimensional values.
profiles.containment: All data marks remain inside the plot domain; labels may move outside a point but stay associated by a non-semantic leader.
profiles.rank_order: Position derives only from quantitative scales; series and label order follow the data contract.
profiles.marks: Axes, ticks, gridlines, point marks, direct labels, and optional disclosed trend or reference line.
profiles.connectors: No point-to-point connectors by default; trend lines and leaders are non-arrowed and explicitly identified.
profiles.reading_order: Title and scale, series legend or direct labels, then observations in data order.
profiles.reflow: Expand domains or canvas and use collision-aware labels without moving point coordinates.
profiles.forbidden: Category card layout, connected observations without series semantics, hidden scale, or radius encoding without a third value.

profiles.arrangement: Source, intermediate, and sink interfaces form ordered columns joined by width-scaled continuous ribbons.
profiles.containment: Ribbons attach within the allocated interface span of their exact source and target nodes.
profiles.rank_order: Flow stages advance in one direction and nodes within a stage are ordered to minimize ribbon crossings.
profiles.marks: Flow node or interface, conserved-width ribbon, value label, and optional stage boundary.
profiles.connectors: Each ribbon is one continuous source-to-target shape whose width encodes amount; arrowheads are unnecessary unless explicitly requested and conservation remains visible.
profiles.reading_order: Source stage through sink stage, then descending flow magnitude or declared order.
profiles.reflow: Grow interfaces and stage gaps while preserving flow amount and conservation.
profiles.forbidden: Uniform thin arrows for quantitative flow, discontinuous ribbons, width drift, or silent loss at junctions.

profiles.arrangement: Ordered collection, processing, and dissemination regions expose current systems and health states across the landscape.
profiles.containment: Systems stay within their functional or trust region and state indicators belong to the system mark.
profiles.rank_order: Operational flow proceeds across regions while legacy, degraded, and active states remain comparable.
profiles.marks: System card with state badge or indicator, region boundary, issue callout, and integration endpoint.
profiles.connectors: Directed rounded orthogonal integration routes attach distributed side ports and distinguish degraded or manual paths without relying only on color.
profiles.reading_order: Region order, then systems by operational flow, then issue annotations.
profiles.reflow: Add systems within the correct region and preserve flow plus state comparison.
profiles.forbidden: Flat dashboard tiles, state conveyed only by color, diagonal integration lines, or system migration implied without evidence.

profiles.arrangement: Participants form fixed columns with headers at the top; lifelines descend and messages are stacked in chronological order.
profiles.containment: Activation bars and combined fragments remain on or across the exact participant span they govern.
profiles.rank_order: Message order strictly descends; nested calls and returns stay adjacent to their invocation.
profiles.marks: Participant header, dashed lifeline, activation bar, message arrow, dashed response, self-call, and optional combined fragment.
profiles.connectors: Straight horizontal sender-to-receiver arrows, dashed response arrows, and rounded self-call returns attach exact lifelines and preserve direction.
profiles.reading_order: Participants left to right, messages top to bottom.
profiles.reflow: Add participants horizontally or messages vertically; never reorder chronology to shorten arrows.
profiles.forbidden: Generic flowchart nodes, diagonal messages, detached arrows, or responses indistinguishable from calls.

profiles.arrangement: Initial dot enters ordered state capsules; terminal bullseye closes the lifecycle and explicit returns occupy a separate outer route.
profiles.containment: Composite-state boundaries, when present, enclose their substates and transitions.
profiles.rank_order: Normal progression advances through state ranks; returns do not pull later states backward.
profiles.marks: Initial dot, rounded state capsule, terminal bullseye, guard label, and state annotation.
profiles.connectors: Directed transition routes attach state boundaries, carry event or guard labels, and separate forward flow from rounded return paths.
profiles.reading_order: Initial state through normal lifecycle, then alternate and return transitions.
profiles.reflow: Add state ranks or return corridors while preserving reachability and transition direction.
profiles.forbidden: Activity-card flowchart, missing initial or terminal state, unlabeled guards, or overlapping return routes.

profiles.arrangement: Entities are compartments arranged by aggregate and relationship structure so cardinality lines stay legible.
profiles.containment: Entity name and attributes remain in one compartment; keys and attribute roles stay attached to their row.
profiles.rank_order: Principal entities precede associative or dependent entities when the model supports that order.
profiles.marks: Entity header, attribute rows, PK or FK markers, relationship label, and independent endpoint cardinalities.
profiles.connectors: Relationship routes bind entity or exact attribute ports and show source and target cardinality independently.
profiles.reading_order: Entities by relationship rank, then attributes top to bottom, then relationships.
profiles.reflow: Grow entities from attribute count and widen gaps for cardinality labels.
profiles.forbidden: Lost endpoint multiplicity, undifferentiated cards, edge labels floating between relations, or crossings treated as junctions.

profiles.arrangement: Equiangular semantic axes radiate from a shared center and each series forms one closed value polygon on a disclosed common scale.
profiles.containment: Series polygons remain within the outer scale ring and axis labels stay outside the plotting field.
profiles.rank_order: Axis order follows the declared domain and is identical for every series.
profiles.marks: Radial axes, scale rings, value vertices, translucent series polygons, and direct or legend labels.
profiles.connectors: Only adjacent values of the same series connect into a closed polygon; no arrows or cross-series junctions.
profiles.reading_order: Axis order around the circle, then series order.
profiles.reflow: Increase radius or label margin and add axes uniformly without changing value mapping.
profiles.forbidden: Unequal undisclosed axes, open profile paths, decorative spokes unrelated to data, or polygon comparison without a common scale.

profiles.arrangement: Cyclical categories occupy ordered angular spokes and magnitude is encoded radially from the shared center.
profiles.containment: Marks and labels respect the circular domain and stay associated with their spoke.
profiles.rank_order: Angular category order follows the declared cycle; radius follows the disclosed quantitative scale.
profiles.marks: Concentric scale rings, category spokes, radial points or sectors, and optional closed series path.
profiles.connectors: A closed path appears only when the data contract treats adjacent cyclical categories as one series; no arrowheads.
profiles.reading_order: Categories around the cycle, then series.
profiles.reflow: Increase radius or label ring and add categories at uniform angular intervals.
profiles.forbidden: Linear bar layout, arbitrary angular order, undisclosed radial scale, or causal arrows between categories.

profiles.arrangement: Stations occupy a balanced ring around a shared center and form one closed reinforcing cycle.
profiles.containment: Optional shared outcome or state sits at the center and does not interrupt the ring.
profiles.rank_order: Station order follows the declared cycle in one direction.
profiles.marks: Cycle station card, central shared-state mark, directional arc, and optional feedback annotation.
profiles.connectors: One continuous directional arc or ordered arc segments connect adjacent station ports and close the loop with consistent arrow direction.
profiles.reading_order: Start at the declared entry station and follow the cycle direction.
profiles.reflow: Increase ring radius or distribute more stations evenly while keeping the closed order.
profiles.forbidden: Open chain, alternating arrow direction, arbitrary hub-and-spoke, or crossed chords used as shortcuts.

profiles.arrangement: Boundaries nest by scope or inheritance depth around a focal core; peer artifacts occupy the innermost valid container.
profiles.containment: Every child is fully inside its declared parent and nested padding remains visually readable.
profiles.rank_order: Outer-to-inner scope depth determines order; artifacts follow stable reading order within a level.
profiles.marks: Nested rounded boundary, scope label, contained artifact card, focal core, and optional inheritance leader.
profiles.connectors: Containment carries the primary meaning; leaders or dependencies appear only when explicitly semantic and do not replace enclosure.
profiles.reading_order: Outermost boundary inward, then contained artifacts.
profiles.reflow: Grow parent bounds from child union and add depth without collapsing padding.
profiles.forbidden: Overlapping peer boxes presented as nesting, child leakage, center-shifted inheritance, or generic cards without enclosure.

profiles.arrangement: One or more roots occupy the top rank and children form centered spans on successive ranks.
profiles.containment: Optional subtree groups contain full descendant branches.
profiles.rank_order: Depth sets rank and stable sibling order preserves the source hierarchy.
profiles.marks: Hierarchy node with consistent role treatment and optional leaf or branch distinction.
profiles.connectors: Parent ports feed an explicit distribution bus or direct child top ports; arrows follow the declared parent-child direction.
profiles.reading_order: Preorder by root and left-to-right siblings.
profiles.reflow: Widen subtree spans or add ranks while preserving parentage and centered alignment.
profiles.forbidden: Force-directed placement, crossing branches, sibling reorder for compactness, or adjacency implied without connectors.

profiles.arrangement: Ordered horizontal layer bands stack from the declared lowest or foundational layer to the highest or experience layer; modules repeat within each band.
profiles.containment: Every module remains fully within one layer and split subdomains stay within their parent band.
profiles.rank_order: Layer order is invariant; module order inside a layer follows request or dependency order.
profiles.marks: Full-width layer band, layer label rail, module cell, focal module, and cross-layer dependency port.
profiles.connectors: Only true cross-layer dependencies use centered vertical or orthogonal routes with direction; adjacency alone is not an edge.
profiles.reading_order: Layer order, then modules left to right within each layer.
profiles.reflow: Increase band height, repeat module columns, or widen canvas without reordering layers.
profiles.forbidden: Floating cards outside bands, layer order drift, arrows for mere stacking, or one generic container around all modules.

profiles.arrangement: Two or three set regions overlap with intentional pairwise and, when applicable, central shared intersections.
profiles.containment: Items or labels occupy only the membership region their semantics permit.
profiles.rank_order: Set order follows the request; overlap depth does not imply priority.
profiles.marks: Equal-status set region, set label, exclusive item, pairwise-overlap item, and shared-intersection item.
profiles.connectors: No semantic connectors; enclosure and overlap alone carry membership.
profiles.reading_order: Set labels, exclusive regions, pairwise overlaps, then central overlap.
profiles.reflow: Change region radius and label positions while preserving all membership intersections.
profiles.forbidden: Non-overlapping circles for shared members, arrows between sets, color-only membership, or arbitrary unequal importance.

profiles.arrangement: Categories share one zero baseline and bars align to a disclosed quantitative axis; grouped series stay adjacent within each category.
profiles.containment: All bars stay inside the plot domain and category labels align to their group.
profiles.rank_order: Category order follows the request or declared sort; series order is consistent across categories.
profiles.marks: Axis, tick, gridline, rectangular bar, value label, and series key or direct label.
profiles.connectors: No semantic connectors or arrowed axes.
profiles.reading_order: Scale, categories in order, then series within category.
profiles.reflow: Expand plot width, wrap category labels, or switch vertical/horizontal orientation while preserving common baseline and values.
profiles.forbidden: Truncated undisclosed baseline, disconnected decorative cards, width encoding when height is claimed, or arrows between bars.

profiles.arrangement: A rectangular parent area is tiled into non-overlapping child rectangles whose areas encode exact nonnegative values.
profiles.containment: Every leaf tile is fully inside its parent group and the child areas partition the available group area.
profiles.rank_order: Group and tile order is stable; area, not position, carries magnitude.
profiles.marks: Group boundary, value-scaled tile, direct label, compact label treatment, and optional focal outline.
profiles.connectors: No semantic connectors; enclosure and area carry hierarchy and magnitude.
profiles.reading_order: Groups then tiles in stable descending or requested order.
profiles.reflow: Retile for canvas shape while preserving area ratios and hierarchy.
profiles.forbidden: Equal-size cards under a quantitative claim, overlapping tiles, gaps counted as data, or arrows between tiles.

profiles.arrangement: Each series follows an ordered shared x-domain across one quantitative plotting field.
profiles.containment: All points and paths stay within the scale domain; direct labels attach to their exact series.
profiles.rank_order: Domain order determines x position and values determine y position; series order remains stable.
profiles.marks: Axes, ticks, gridlines, series path, data points, missing-value gap, and direct or legend label.
profiles.connectors: Only consecutive valid points of the same series connect; missing values break the path and no arrowheads are used.
profiles.reading_order: Domain left to right, then series order.
profiles.reflow: Extend domain or canvas and reposition labels without changing point coordinates or gap semantics.
profiles.forbidden: Smoothed invented values, connected missing points, category cards, or trend arrows unrelated to data.

profiles.arrangement: Tasks occupy rows against one calendar scale; each bar spans its exact start and end and milestones sit at their date.
profiles.containment: Tasks remain in their phase or workstream group and bars stay inside the calendar plot.
profiles.rank_order: Row order follows phase or dependency order; horizontal position follows time only.
profiles.marks: Time header, task row, duration bar, progress fill, milestone, phase band, and dependency endpoint.
profiles.connectors: Dependencies attach exact task boundaries and route outside bars with directional arrowheads; the calendar grid is non-semantic.
profiles.reading_order: Calendar scale, phases, then task rows top to bottom.
profiles.reflow: Extend date range and add rows or phase bands without distorting duration.
profiles.forbidden: Equal-width bars for unequal durations, dependencies through labels, date reorder, or progress conveyed only by color.

profiles.arrangement: Major stages progress left to right inside a bounded overview, with cross-cutting governance or capabilities shown as a separate spanning band.
profiles.containment: Stage services remain inside their stage and the spanning band stays visually distinct from the stage flow.
profiles.rank_order: Primary stages retain their declared order; shared concerns do not become an extra process step.
profiles.marks: Stage boundary, service card, focal platform card, cross-cutting band, and concise annotation.
profiles.connectors: Simple directed stage routes use rounded orthogonal corners and exact side ports; cross-cutting coverage is not drawn as a dependency edge.
profiles.reading_order: Stage progression, then shared band and annotations.
profiles.reflow: Widen stages or stack services within a stage while preserving the overview sequence.
profiles.forbidden: Flat card grid, governance as a false terminal stage, diagonal routes, or silent stage reorder.

profiles.arrangement: A primary process spine advances through role-specific activity, decision, document, data, and terminal marks with explicit branches or returns.
profiles.containment: Optional phases or owners contain complete steps and keep artifact marks with their producer or consumer.
profiles.rank_order: Step order follows the source; branches retain guard order and returns use an outer corridor.
profiles.marks: Activity, decision, document, data store, start or end, annotation, and artifact marks remain visually distinct.
profiles.connectors: Directed centered or orthogonal routes attach role-aware ports, carry guards on their own edge, and preserve continuity.
profiles.reading_order: Primary process order, then branch alternatives and returns.
profiles.reflow: Add ranks, phase space, or branch width without replacing role-specific marks with cards.
profiles.forbidden: Single card vocabulary, unlabeled branch, discontinuous route, or crossing that looks like a merge.

profiles.arrangement: Data lifecycle or quality tiers appear as an ordered stack or nested promotion sequence from raw intake through curated serving.
profiles.containment: Assets and controls stay within their tier and processing paths bridge only the tiers they actually transform.
profiles.rank_order: Promotion order is invariant and failure or recycle paths remain visibly separate.
profiles.marks: Tier band, dataset or service card, quality gate, promotion arrow, and processing-path annotation.
profiles.connectors: Directed promotions connect adjacent or explicitly skipped tiers at centered ports; alternate processing paths are distinct and labeled.
profiles.reading_order: Earliest or raw tier through final serving tier, then alternate paths.
profiles.reflow: Add tier height or repeated assets while preserving promotion order.
profiles.forbidden: Unordered colored cards, tier names used only as legend, arrowless promotion, or recycle path mistaken for forward flow.

profiles.arrangement: Source systems occupy the left, the data-platform boundary owns ingestion, processing, storage, and serving services in the center, and consumers occupy the right; shared services form a distinct cross-cutting area.
profiles.containment: Every platform service stays inside the platform boundary while sources and consumers stay outside; shared services remain clearly owned.
profiles.rank_order: Lineage proceeds source to platform service ranks to consumer, with platform subflow preserved.
profiles.marks: Source, ingestion, transform, store, serving, consumer, shared-service card, and platform boundary.
profiles.connectors: Boundary-aware directed orthogonal routes use distributed east-west ports, retain exact source-target lineage, and separate control from data paths.
profiles.reading_order: Sources, platform subflow, consumers, then shared services.
profiles.reflow: Stack peers within their stage and grow the platform boundary without flattening ownership.
profiles.forbidden: One middle generic box, sources inside platform, unbound boundary crossings, or merged data and control paths.

profiles.arrangement: Actors or roles form rows, resources or platform components form columns, and each intersection shows one explicit permission state.
profiles.containment: Every state mark stays inside exactly one row-column cell; headers align across the full grid.
profiles.rank_order: Row and column order follows the access model and remains stable across modes.
profiles.marks: Row header, column header, grid cell, permission glyph plus text label, and optional group separator.
profiles.connectors: No semantic connectors; row-column position carries the relation.
profiles.reading_order: Column headers, then each role row left to right.
profiles.reflow: Add rows or columns and enable horizontal expansion while preserving cell alignment.
profiles.forbidden: Loose permission cards, state conveyed only by color, missing cell labels, or arrows between role and resource.

profiles.arrangement: One horizontal cause spine terminates at the effect; category bones angle into the spine and individual causes branch from their category bone.
profiles.containment: Each cause stays attached to exactly one named category branch.
profiles.rank_order: Categories distribute along the spine and causes follow stable order along each branch.
profiles.marks: Effect head, main spine, category bone, cause twig, category label, and cause label.
profiles.connectors: Angled category bones terminate on the shared spine and cause twigs terminate on their category bone; direction converges toward the effect without arrow clutter.
profiles.reading_order: Categories from spine start to effect, then causes per category.
profiles.reflow: Lengthen the spine and space branches or causes while preserving convergence.
profiles.forbidden: Mind-map radial layout, floating causes, category branches crossing, or multiple undeclared effects.

profiles.arrangement: Components occupy a two-dimensional field with visibility on the vertical axis and evolution on the horizontal axis.
profiles.containment: All components remain inside the disclosed field and evolution-stage bands retain their order.
profiles.rank_order: Coordinates come from strategy values; vertical dependency chains remain readable.
profiles.marks: Evolution stage band, positioned component, focal component, direct label, and optional movement annotation.
profiles.connectors: Dependency routes connect exact component ports without arrowheads unless direction is explicitly material; movement arrows are visually distinct.
profiles.reading_order: Axes and stages, then value chain from visible need downward, then evolution position.
profiles.reflow: Expand field or move labels while preserving semantic coordinates and dependencies.
profiles.forbidden: Quadrant substitution, arbitrary coordinates, dependency and movement conflation, or crossings treated as junctions.

profiles.arrangement: Workflow states form ordered vertical columns with WIP counts or limits in headers and work items stacked inside their current column.
profiles.containment: Every item belongs to exactly one status column and blocked or waiting flags remain attached to the card.
profiles.rank_order: Column order follows workflow; card order follows priority or request order without implying duration.
profiles.marks: Column boundary and header, WIP indicator, work card, assignee or tag, blocked flag, and done state.
profiles.connectors: No connectors by default; column position carries state and movement is not invented.
profiles.reading_order: Columns left to right, cards top to bottom.
profiles.reflow: Add columns or card rows and grow board width while preserving WIP and status.
profiles.forbidden: Flowchart arrows between every card, cards outside columns, hidden WIP breach, or status conveyed only by color.

profiles.arrangement: Classes are compartments arranged to expose inheritance, composition, aggregation, and association with minimal crossings.
profiles.containment: Class name, attributes, and operations remain in distinct ordered compartments.
profiles.rank_order: Superclasses precede subclasses; collaborating peers align on the same rank when possible.
profiles.marks: Class header, attribute and operation rows with visibility, stereotype, abstract marker, and relationship endpoint symbols.
profiles.connectors: Typed UML relationship routes bind exact class ports, preserve arrow or diamond endpoint semantics, and show multiplicity independently at both ends.
profiles.reading_order: Inheritance hierarchy, then class compartments top to bottom, then peer relations.
profiles.reflow: Grow classes from member count and add hierarchy ranks without detaching endpoints.
profiles.forbidden: Generic entity boxes, wrong diamond ownership, missing multiplicity, or relationship crossings treated as merge.

profiles.arrangement: Backbone activities form ordered columns across the top and stories align beneath their activity in release-slice rows separated by explicit cuts.
profiles.containment: Every story belongs to one backbone activity and one release slice; risk markers remain attached to the story.
profiles.rank_order: Backbone order follows user activity; release slices progress top to bottom.
profiles.marks: Backbone activity card, story card, release-slice band, MVP or release cutline, and risk marker.
profiles.connectors: No connectors by default; column and row position carry activity and release membership.
profiles.reading_order: Backbone left to right, then stories by release slice top to bottom.
profiles.reflow: Add activities, stories, or release rows while preserving both axes and cuts.
profiles.forbidden: Kanban status columns, process arrows between stories, stories crossing activity columns, or hidden release cut.

profiles.arrangement: Categories form rows on one shared quantitative axis; each row has exactly two endpoint marks joined by one comparison segment.
profiles.containment: Both endpoints, gap label, and category label remain associated with the same row.
profiles.rank_order: Category row order follows request or declared sort; endpoint semantics stay consistent across rows.
profiles.marks: Shared axis, category label, first-state dot, second-state dot, connecting segment, and signed gap label.
profiles.connectors: One non-arrowed segment per category connects only its paired endpoints; it is a comparison mark, not flow.
profiles.reading_order: Scale, then category rows top to bottom and endpoints in declared state order.
profiles.reflow: Add rows or expand the shared domain while preserving one pair per category.
profiles.forbidden: Separate bars, unpaired dots, arrows suggesting flow, inconsistent state side, or per-row independent scales.

profiles.arrangement: Exactly two ordered state columns share one quantitative scale and each series is one straight endpoint-to-endpoint slope.
profiles.containment: Direct labels stay attached to their endpoint side and ties or ranks remain explicit.
profiles.rank_order: Vertical position derives from value; label layout preserves rank and crossing visibility.
profiles.marks: Two state rails, paired endpoints, straight slope segment, direct series labels, delta or rank annotation.
profiles.connectors: One non-arrowed straight segment per series; crossings mean rank change, never junction.
profiles.reading_order: Left state top to bottom, follow each series to the right state, then compare ranks.
profiles.reflow: Increase height or label gutters for collisions while preserving endpoint values and crossings.
profiles.forbidden: More than two states under this profile, curved trend lines, arrowheads, merged crossings, or independent scales.

profiles.arrangement: Distribution series form vertically offset parallel ridges over one shared horizontal domain and one disclosed amplitude normalization contract.
profiles.containment: Each filled or stroked density remains in its labeled row while intentional overlap stays controlled.
profiles.rank_order: Ridge row order follows request and x position uses the same domain for every series.
profiles.marks: Shared x-axis, ridge baseline, density shape, row label, and optional percentile or interval marker.
profiles.connectors: Density paths are closed or baseline-terminated shapes, not semantic connectors; no arrows or cross-ridge junctions.
profiles.reading_order: Shared domain, then ridges top to bottom.
profiles.reflow: Add ridge rows or increase row spacing without changing the shared scale or normalization.
profiles.forbidden: Separate per-row domains, arbitrary amplitude, ordinary multi-line chart, or connecting ridges.

profiles.arrangement: Observations occupy exact x-y positions and a third nonnegative magnitude controls circle area on a disclosed size scale.
profiles.containment: Bubble centers remain inside the x-y plot domain and labels avoid covering smaller bubbles.
profiles.rank_order: Position follows x and y; overlap order follows a declared size or label policy without changing values.
profiles.marks: Axes, gridlines, area-scaled circle, direct label, size legend, and optional reference line.
profiles.connectors: No point-to-point connectors; leaders and reference lines are non-arrowed and declared.
profiles.reading_order: Axes and size legend, then observations in stable order.
profiles.reflow: Expand domains, canvas, or label gutters while preserving centers and area ratios.
profiles.forbidden: Radius proportional to value when area is claimed, arbitrary positions, missing size legend, or connected bubbles.

profiles.arrangement: Broad full-width horizontal bands form a simple abstraction stack with one optional non-color focal layer and a disclosed low-to-high abstraction axis.
profiles.containment: Layer descriptions stay inside their band; this presentation does not add module compartments unless the user selects type-layer-stack instead.
profiles.rank_order: Layer order follows the declared abstraction or responsibility progression and remains invariant across modes.
profiles.marks: Layer band, layer name, concise description, focal outline or side rail, and abstraction-axis annotation.
profiles.connectors: No inter-layer arrows by default; stacking and the axis express order.
profiles.reading_order: Declared bottom-to-top or top-to-bottom layer order, stated explicitly.
profiles.reflow: Add bands or increase band height while keeping full-width alignment and order.
profiles.forbidden: Module grid substitution, arrows between every layer, color-only focus, or silent order reversal.

profiles.arrangement: Independent observations occupy exact x-y coordinates in a conventional scatter plot with an optional disclosed fitted trend across the shared domain.
profiles.containment: Points remain within the plot field and direct labels or the trend annotation stay associated without moving points.
profiles.rank_order: Positions derive only from the two scales; label priority and draw order do not alter values.
profiles.marks: Axes, ticks, gridlines, hollow or solid observation point, direct focal label, and distinct fitted trend line.
profiles.connectors: Observations are not connected; the fitted trend is non-arrowed, visually distinct, and labeled as a model rather than an observed path.
profiles.reading_order: Axes and units, observations in data order, then fitted trend and focal annotation.
profiles.reflow: Expand domains, canvas, or label gutters while preserving coordinates and recomputing only an explicitly requested fit.
profiles.forbidden: Connected time-series path, invented trend, hidden axes, arrowed regression, or point relocation for aesthetics.
